taxonomy.subtopic: Medial longitudinal fasciculus connection between abducens interneurons and contralateral medial rectus nucleus

questions.stem_html: A 26-year-old woman with relapsing neurologic symptoms develops horizontal diplopia. During attempted right gaze, the right eye abducts with nystagmus, but the left eye fails to adduct. Both eyes converge normally on a near target. The accompanying gaze-circuit diagram shows the interrupted pathway. Which structure is damaged?

options.text_html: Left medial longitudinal fasciculus between the right abducens nucleus and left oculomotor nucleus
Left oculomotor nerve fascicle supplying the medial rectus muscle
Right medial longitudinal fasciculus between the left abducens nucleus and right oculomotor nucleus
Left abducens nerve after it exits the pons

questions.explanation_html: For rightward gaze, the right abducens nucleus activates the right lateral rectus and sends internuclear axons across the midline into the left medial longitudinal fasciculus. These fibers ascend to the left oculomotor medial-rectus subnucleus. A left medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion therefore impairs left-eye adduction during rightward gaze while sparing direct convergence pathways; compensatory excess drive produces nystagmus of the abducting right eye.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: A left oculomotor fascicular lesion would usually impair both adduction and convergence and may affect additional third-nerve functions.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: A right pontine horizontal gaze-center lesion would impair conjugate gaze of both eyes to the right, including right-eye abduction.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: A right medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion causes impaired right-eye adduction during leftward gaze.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: A left abducens nerve lesion prevents left-eye abduction, not left-eye adduction during right gaze.

questions.educational_objective: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia localizes to the medial longitudinal fasciculus ipsilateral to the eye with impaired adduction; convergence may remain intact.

media.alt_text: Original horizontal gaze circuit showing the right abducens nucleus, crossing internuclear fibers, left medial longitudinal fasciculus, and interruption causing left internuclear ophthalmoplegia.
